- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained upward trends.
- After a sharp price spike, model underreacts and fails to capture the continuation or reversal momentum.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model assumes prices will return to historical averages too quickly.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher values, suggesting model lacks sensitivity to recent downward momentum or policy shocks.
- Model underestimates late-period price surges (e.g., final 5–10 days of forecast often lag behind true outcomes).
- Overshoots after spikes are common — model reacts too aggressively to short-term volatility, then corrects too early.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or policy-driven price shifts (e.g., ETS auction cycles, regulatory changes) in the forecast window.
